facts.text: Avilla began in 1881 when German settlers from Saxony founded Hope Colony, a community built around communal farming and Lutheran worship.
The Iron Mountain Railroad’s post‑Civil War advertisements attracted Saxon immigrants, prompting the establishment of a communal log house and Zion Evangelical Lutheran Church in 1881.
Before the Civil War, pioneers received federal land grants—such as Henry Fletcher in 1834 and Thomas Keesee in 1839—to clear timber and farm in northern Saline County.
Early Avilla economy focused on clearing land for cotton, corn, cabbage, livestock, and subsistence crops, with community celebrations on holidays like Christmas and Independence Day.
The Zion Evangelical Lutheran Church and School, founded in 1881, conducted services and education entirely in German until the 1940s, reflecting the community’s heritage.
In the early 2000s, Avilla Christian Academy emerged from the Lutheran school to attract a diverse student body, while the church added a food pantry and community garden.
